versions.short: The law expands the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program, which help farmers and private forest owners pay for repairs and emergency work after natural disasters. It lets producers receive advance payments covering part of the cost of replacing, repairing, or restoring farmland and conservation structures that need an immediate response, and lets owners of private forest land receive an advance of up to 75% of emergency work costs. Recipients now have 180 days to use program funds instead of 60 days for the conservation program. The programs also now cover damage from some wildfires, including those with unnatural causes that spread due to natural conditions and those caused by the federal government.
